I’ve been banking with CIBC since the day I moved to Canada, but unfortunately my recent experiences at this branch have been extremely disappointing.

Almost every time I visit, there is a huge lineup, often with only one or two employees serving customers. I’ve waited 45 minutes to an hour, only to eventually be told, “You have to call the online team.” If customers are consistently being redirected elsewhere after waiting that long, then what is the purpose of having in-person service?

I also want to mention the behaviour of the security guard. I have personally noticed a very different attitude toward white customers compared with brown customers. She appears friendly and welcoming toward some customers, while at times barely acknowledging or engaging with brown customers. As a brown customer, that treatment is uncomfortable and makes me feel unwelcome.

I have been loyal to CIBC for years, and I believe they can do much better. Customers deserve to be treated with respect, regardless of their background, and they deserve reasonable wait times and actual assistance when they come into a branch.

I hope CIBC takes this feedback seriously and works on improving both the customer service and the way customers are treated.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very very rarely do I give a negative review, but this place deserves it and more!

Public access to the lake in Ste‑Marguerite‑du‑Lac‑Masson is surprisingly difficult — honestly, I find more accessible nature in a big city than in this village. We tried to use the city ramp with already‑washed paddleboards, but still needed the city’s pink sticker, which felt like les 12 travaux d’Astérix. We were sent to the village garage, which was poorly indicated and completely closed. Back at the marina, staff tried calling with no answer. Only after returning again and finding someone half‑asleep at the garage were we finally able to get on the water — hours later. For a lakeside village, this level of disorganization is really disappointing. And this was the only place were we could access the water on the whole lake!!!

This was one of the first times where I felt the saying ''beeing poor is more expensive'' to be true. For those reading this, think about the society we live in, where access to nature is for the rich! And mind me not, this will only get worse...we need a revolution were people are being granted access to nature!

Months ago I dropped off 3 milwaukee batteries for testing for warranty my rep told me they had to be tested here first. I'm now told no we won't be returning your batteries to you as that was only for new ones not the used ones when denied. I told them how I checked and clarified all this at the start and it was insisted that in either event they would deliver them back to me no issues at all, again I'm told no they won't be delivering them and theres nothing they will do.
Warranty denial aside this dealer has provided one of the worst customer service experiences I've had to date.

Very disappointed with my mother’s experience with this company.

In April 2026, we received a letter from IRCC advising that my mother’s application had been refused. Since then, we repeatedly asked the consultant to take action regarding the refusal. Her response was that we should disregard the letter because IRCC had subsequently sent a recall notice, and that my mother should simply wait to be contacted again.

As an experienced and licensed immigration professional, she should know that immigration matters are time-sensitive. When we asked about contacting IRCC directly, she advised that there was no way to speak with an officer. However, I was able to contact IRCC by telephone on multiple occasions to obtain information about my mother's file while she continued to advise us to wait.

She was also aware that, following a refusal, there is a limited period in which an application for judicial review may be filed. We discussed these deadlines, yet no action was taken. Had we followed her advice and continued waiting, we could have lost the opportunity to pursue available remedies.

I am concerned that my mom’s application was not handled with the level of diligence and urgency that it required. I do not understand why, instead of addressing these concerns, she simply chose to become defensive and withdraw from my mom’s case.

In reviewing my mother’s application materials, I was also disappointed by the quality of the submissions prepared on her behalf. I found the language and presentation to be unprofessional and insufficiently persuasive, which has left us feeling that our time, trust, and money were not well invested. ChatGPT would have done a better job!

I absolutely do not recommend this company!

I was disappointed with my experience at Axess Law. I was interested in having a Will and Powers of Attorney prepared and specifically went to the Scarborough Town Centre location after seeing their advertised $349 Will & Powers of Attorney package.

Unfortunately, I found the communication quite confusing. The Asian lady I spoke with explained things very quickly, and despite asking questions, I left without a clear understanding of exactly what the service included or how the process worked. I had also previously gone to this location because Google indicated that it was open on a Sunday, only to find that it was actually closed. I subsequently called before returning.

The pricing is certainly attractive compared with many estate law firms, but I think the distinction between preparing Will/POA documents and providing actual estate-planning advice needs to be communicated much more clearly. I ultimately decided not to proceed because I did not feel confident that I fully understood the service I would be receiving.

Hopefully Axess can improve the clarity of its communication and make it easier for clients to understand exactly what is and is not included before they make the trip to the office.

The reviews definitely match the shitty service I received today.

My husband had been hit by a car while on a scooter and was lying injured, and I was desperately asking this guy to get out of his truck and assess him. 911 told me they were going to drop the call because these guys were trained to deal with medical situations, so I expected them to actually help.

Instead, this guy sat in his truck laughing in my face while I was begging him to come help my husband. He had his headphones in, kept giggling, and repeatedly asked me where my husband was instead of actually listening to me. I told him multiple times where he was, and he still didn’t seem interested in helping. Eventually, he walked away.

They finally followed me to where my husband was laying, which is exactly what they should have done from the beginning. Then, instead of taking responsibility for the fact that he had ignored me, he decided to tell me that I seemed like I didn’t know how to handle a stressful situation.

Yeah, no kidding, I was dealing with my husband being hit by a car while you were standing there laughing in my face and refusing to listen or help. I was stressed because of the situation. You were the one who wasn’t doing your job.

I told him again that I had already told him where my husband was multiple times. He then tried to argue with me over whether I had said it three times or five times, saying, “Oh, it went from three times to five times?” At that point, I had told him repeatedly and in multiple ways where my husband was. If you still weren’t getting it, it clearly wasn’t because I wasn’t communicating, it was because you weren’t listening.

Me telling him that I recorded him laughing on my Ai glasses was what got his attention and kept wanted to see this instead of doing this job still. His three partners ended up cleaning my husband up while he stood around trying to see my glasses.

He didn’t want to give me his information and instead told me to go look at his truck. I’m fully aware that when 911 dispatches a fire team to a scene, they are informed of why they are being sent there and what they are responding to. Yet this guy acted like a complete fool and pretended he had no idea why he was there or what was happening. It seemed like they didn’t wanna get out of their trucks and it was an inconvenience for them to be there.

The lack of professionalism, empathy, and urgency was absolutely disgusting. When someone is injured after being hit by a car, the last thing they should have to do is beg for help while a supposedly trained professional laughs in their face.

Absolutely unacceptable service.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve tried this yoga studio several times over the past few years, and unfortunately, my experiences have become increasingly disappointing.
My last class was particularly uncomfortable, hence why I haven’t returned since. The instructor had a very aggressive approach and repeatedly encouraged people to push through discomfort and avoid making adjustments. That kind of messaging feels inappropriate in a class attended by people with different bodies, abilities, experience levels, and reasons for practicing yoga. I left feeling that the atmosphere prioritized intensity and compliance over body awareness, accessibility, and individual choice.
Since then I stayed connected through subscribing through their emails in case I wanted to reapproach this space, however, I’ve also found the frequent emails about “etiquette” increasingly excessive. The most recent one actually stated: “Please come to class in clean workout clothing and, when possible, arrive freshly showered. Deodorant is always appreciated.” While basic consideration for others is reasonable, the tone and frequency of these reminders create a surprisingly rigid culture around what should ultimately be a welcoming, inclusive fitness space.
There is also a socioeconomic dimension to expectations like this that I don’t think the studio has considered. Not everyone has the ability to shower immediately before and after exercise, change into fresh workout clothes, or structure their day around these expectations. Presenting these things as norms can quickly become exclusionary and alienating.
Overall, I think the studio would benefit from reconsidering the culture it is creating: less policing, less emphasis on pushing through discomfort, and more emphasis on autonomy, inclusivity, accessibility, and meeting people where they are. Yoga should be a space where people feel welcome—not a place where they feel they have to conform to an increasingly narrow set of expectations.

one_star_reviews.text: Been waiting for 12 hours -- I have a probable blood clot and have been kept waiting this long -- and the highlight of my visit has been watching the triage nurse fall asleep while patients were trying to ask questions. (Then, when she saw she'd been caught, she made a big deal about cleaning up her desk. Hilarious.) Note: Finally brought in for tests after 16 hours.

Worst experience at a hospital EVER. I presented with symptoms of an antibiotic resistant infection with a large mass on my jawline. Instead of being taken seriously my reasoning written down was “dental issues” despite being told I was 48 hours unable to hold down food, on 6 days of antibiotics and the infection was growing and expanding by the minute. I arrived at 10AMand was waiting in their waiting room until 7:30 PM when I showed up it was supposed to be an hour and a half wait time but because she put me as a “dental” and not wrote down the SERIOUS infection signs and symptoms that could have easily turned into sepsis while in this waiting room. During my time in the waiting room I was immobilized by pain and nausea, meanwhile I witnessed a man in a suit and tie across from me pacing the room and eating a large Tim Hortons lunch. Despite being there BEFORE this man he was called before me. When I went up to the nurses to ask how much longer I was told “it’s based on sickness” so you’re telling me a man who is standing up, walking around, eating and drinking NORMALLY AND FINE is MORE SICK then the person who has been unable to keep food down for 48 hours, was swelling more and more by the hour and by the time I was finally called into a waiting room my jaw was ready to burst open. I was not taken seriously until someone else showed up with me and told the nurses “you need to listen, she has a grapefruit sized lump in her neck, burning all the way down, unable to keep food down for multiple days and has an active infection” finally they checked my name to see that YES I HAD BEEN THERE THE LONGEST and yet somehow NOBODY HAD SEEN ME YET? finally when I was put into a room I was shoved into a corner and after more hours in the room I was transferred to another hospital for immediate surgery for the extreme infection. These triage nurses should be ashamed of how they treat people, I kindly asked how long it would be to be rudely shoved aside and told I wasn’t sick enough when I was one of the sickest people in that room all day and was ignored.

On top of that, the lady at the desk when you walk in is useless. She’s supposed to be a nurse but does nothing. She watched a patient actively seizing in front of her and didn’t even stand up from her desk to help when the woman’s daughter was screaming for help.
Worst experience I’ve ever had in an emergency room ever, never have I been treated so awfully and shoved aside when my infection could and would have turned deadly.

I went in to return a dress we had purchased because it didn’t fit my sister properly. The dress also had makeup stains on it when it was sold to us. Beyond the policy itself, the way the situation was handled was extremely disappointing. The employee at the cash was rude, snappy, lacked empathy, and made no effort to help resolve an issue caused by the store selling us a stained item in the first place.

I wish I had gotten her name at the time, but I will be calling the store to find out because the way this was handled was not acceptable. Very disappointing experience.

They were very quick at taking a deposit and told me my window would be ready within a month. They were the ones who made it the year before so they had the measurements.. I called back a month later and they could not find my information and eventually they stumbled on a not saying “to measure”. They explained that they had to come measure the window to make sure, but they couldn’t give me a date because they are not operating “in my area” right now. I live in the same city and it is a 12 minute drive. Eventually someone cane to measure, told me it should take a couple of weeks for everything to be done and left. I called back after a few weeks, asked for a date; I was told some time this week or the next one. At the end of the second week, I called back the seller — at this point we were on a first name basis — and told him I needed an installation date. He got angry, lost patience, asked me if I wanted my deposit back and try with some other place else (as if he had a monopoly on windows… his competitor is across the street!), telling me that they could not do it faster. I said yes. On the first day of the following week, he called back, acting nice, saying it could be done either Thursday or Friday and I could choose the time. I asked for the first thing on Thursday. Well, the following day, one hour after their closing time, I received a voicemail saying my new window broke while they put it in the truck.

I called back first thing the next business day and asked for my deposit back (there was no more window anyway!), but they wouldn’t give it back because “that’s not how it works” and “we probably already passed the order” (as if they ever did anything fast. I had to drive there, asked to see the seller, sit for 5 seconds while introducing myself and asked for my money back. The seller, of all people, cursed me out of his office telling the secretary to give me back my money (making me sound like a beggar for scraps). Before leaving, I asked to see the owner to give some feedback. She, then, told me I had just talked to him… The clown is running the circus.

From passing my order, to deliver and customer service, no one was competent except the receptionist! They took 4 months to measure,  manufacture and subsequently destroy a single window.

I went to get my window manufactured and installed somewhere else very close and they did everything in less time then it took Fenetre St-Paul to come measure my window. Customer service was good and the price was roughly the same.

one_star_reviews.text:
We found CertaPro through Google and decided to give them a try for what seemed like a simple job, given the high ratings. Unfortunately, our experience didn't match that reputation.

During the estimate, we were told matching the existing color would be no problem. On the second day, the painter suggested a color that wasn't close to the original at all — but showed us a photo that looked close, so we approved it. When we saw the actual result that evening, we contacted Mike right away, since we were relying on his team's expertise to get the color matching right.

We were then asked to visit the paint shop ourselves the next morning to sort out the color — which took several trips and still didn't get us the right match. Eventually the painter joined us at the store and helped resolve it. But afterward, we were told that because we had "requested" the color change, the second coat of the new color wouldn't be covered under the contract.

We trusted their expertise to get this right, but it felt like the priority was squeezing extra fees rather than standing behind their own recommendation. The painter advised that a third coat was recommended even before the job is completed since some areas were looking patchy — but of course needed to charge extra for it, on top of everything.

Maybe that's standard in the trade, but it didn't feel like the promises made at the estimate were kept particularly  when it comes to the color we requested since the beginning. Had we changed our minds on the color, then I would agree what they are asking is fair, but the color of choice never changed. Now with the remaining paint, we'll complete the "third" coat ourselves but we wouldn't recommend CertaPro based on our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was the person at home dealing with most of the contractors and subcontractors during our basement renovation, and the entire experience was incredibly frustrating from the beginning.
Even getting the project started was difficult. After hiring Hope Construction, weeks went by with little to no communication. We repeatedly had to call and message just to find out when someone was coming. There were long stretches where nobody showed up, nobody called, and we had no idea what was happening with our own renovation.
Once work started, the biggest issue was the lack of coordination. Different trades would arrive and often seemed unclear about exactly what they were supposed to be doing. From my perspective, there was no consistent foreman or representative from Hope Construction onsite managing the work. It often felt like a trade had simply been called and sent over without being properly briefed on the actual plan.
That lack of communication led to unnecessary and incorrect work. A ceiling was textured that we did not want textured, a vent was covered that should not have been covered, and holes were made in walls where they were not supposed to be. There were multiple times where work had to be questioned, corrected, or redone because the people onsite did not appear to have been given clear direction….
We had also purchased many of our own materials and supplies. Contractors would come in and use materials that belonged to us, and we also discovered items and supplies missing during the project. When we later asked Hope about these things, we were left with very few answers.
Another major concern was the permits. We were charged for the building permit process, but when we checked with the City, we were advised that permits had not been obtained. When we questioned Hope about why we were being charged for permits that had not been pulled, their representative became upset and raised their voice at us instead of simply explaining the situation.
The cleaning was another disappointment. We were charged for final cleaning, yet cleaners were sent while the renovation was nowhere near finished. Construction continued afterward, and we were ultimately left with dust, dirt and construction mess that we had to clean ourselves.
What stands out most to me is how little communication and supervision there was throughout the project. We should not have had to constantly chase the company for updates, explain the job to trades ourselves, or catch mistakes that proper onsite management should have prevented.
More than a year after hiring the company, the basement was still not properly finished.
This is my firsthand experience as the homeowner who was here dealing with the project day to day. Unfortunately, based on that experience, I cannot recommend Hope Construction.

UPDATE: I stand by my review because it reflects what I personally experienced while being home and dealing with this project day to day.
My concerns were specific… long periods with little communication, trades arriving unexpectedly & without clear direction, very little onsite supervision from Hope Construction, mistakes that had to be corrected, our own materials being used, permit concerns, cleaning issues, and a basement that remained unfinished more than a year later.
I also want to clarify the suggestion that we have been unwilling to resolve this… A detailed formal dispute was sent on July 8 outlining the outstanding issues, and there was no substantive response for nearly two months. Hope Construction has now acknowledged our latest response and advised that they will provide a more detailed reply next week.
We are absolutely willing to review a genuine proposal to resolve this. I would much rather see the basement properly finished and the financial issues dealt with fairly than continue arguing publicly.
My review is not “bashing.” It is my honest account of what I personally experienced in my own home.

⭐️ Very disappointing experience — especially regarding Ontario Seniors Dental Coverage

I brought my father in for his dental appointment because he has dental coverage through the Ontario Seniors Dental Care Program. At the beginning of the appointment, we were told that the necessary work would be covered. Based on that information, we proceeded with the appointment expecting the treatment to be completed as explained.

Unfortunately, the appointment felt extremely rushed. They only completed the work on his bottom teeth and then told us we would need to return another day to have the upper teeth done. We were then told that the upper portion would not be covered, and that we would have to pay the full price for that portion of the treatment.

What was particularly frustrating was that we were initially told the treatment would be covered, only to find out afterward that completing the other half would result in a significant out-of-pocket expense.

We were also told that the reason the appointment could not be completed was because the clinic gives everyone a standard one-hour appointment. However, when I got back to my car and checked the time, I realized that my father’s actual treatment had only taken approximately 39 minutes.

I understand that appointments can have time limitations and that coverage has specific rules, but the communication and handling of this appointment were very disappointing. If there were limitations on what could be completed or what was covered, that should have been clearly explained before treatment began, rather than leaving us to discover afterward that additional work would come with a full charge.

I hope the clinic can improve its communication with seniors and their families, particularly when patients are relying on government-funded dental coverage and are being told that their treatment is covered.

Formal Complaint Regarding Veterinary Services and Health Certificate

I am extremely disappointed with the service I received from this clinic while preparing my two cats for international travel.

I have spent more than $1,600 at this clinic in total. I paid approximately $500 for both cats to receive their microchips and vaccinations,  also spent a significant amount of money on airline tickets, health examinations, and other travel arrangements. I had been planning this trip and preparing all of the required documents for approximately two months.

Unfortunately, the health certificate printed by the clinic staff was incomplete.  Bottom  grade was got cut off. Because of this error, the CFIA was unable to endorse the health certificate. I was therefore required to return to the clinic and request that a new, complete health certificate be printed and properly completed by the veterinarian who examined and named my cats . Callie.

However, the veterinarian refused to complete the certificate again and made comments that I found threatening and extremely inappropriate. I was eventually told that I would have to pick up the document after the clinic had closed, using the back door. Alternatively, the clinic offered to refund only $11 and refused to sign the health certificate.

This situation has caused me considerable stress, inconvenience, and additional expenses. I had to travel back and forth between the clinic and the CFIA because of a mistake made by the clinic staff when the original health certificate was printed incorrectly.

What is even more frustrating is that the receptionist refused to acknowledge that the clinic staff had made a mistake. I was told, “We were not supposed to print the health certificate.” This is extremely concerning because I relied on the clinic to provide the documentation necessary for my cats to travel.I paid 500 for the exames and required the healthy certificate for the CFIA  endorsement.

I understand that mistakes can happen, but I expect a veterinary clinic to take responsibility for its mistakes and work with its clients to resolve them fast  —especially when those mistakes can jeopardize an international trip involving significant expenses and extensive preparation.

Instead, I felt that my concerns were dismissed and that I was treated as though my situation was not important. I have spent more than $1,600 at this clinic, yet I was left feeling that my business and the time, money, and effort I invested in preparing my cats for travel were not appreciated.

This experience has been extremely upsetting and has made an already stressful travel process much more difficult than it needed to be. I am requesting that the clinic review what happened, including the incomplete health certificate, the staff's handling of the situation, and the veterinarian's refusal to correct the documentation.

I hope the clinic will take responsibility for the inconvenience and difficulties caused by this situation and provide an appropriate resolution.

one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give negative stars I would. I had an extremely unpleasant experience with the receptionist at this clinic. I understand that clinics can be busy and staff may be occupied, but there is no reason for a patient to be spoken to or treated this way.

When I arrived, the receptionist did not acknowledge me or let me know that she would be with me shortly. I could see that she was busy, so I waited patiently for several minutes without interrupting her. When I eventually tried to get her attention, she simply and rudely said, “Wait,” without any other acknowledgement. I then continued waiting for another few minutes.

When she was finally ready to assist me, I handed her my requisition form and OHIP card, which she abruptly took from my hand while appearing visibly annoyed. After reviewing my requisition, she told me I would need to come back in the morning because one of the tests indicated “AM.” I explained that I had already fasted and had not eaten, and simply asked whether that made any difference. Her response was, “I already said come back in the morning,” with no further explanation.

I continued asking questions because I was trying to understand what time I needed to return and which specific test required a morning appointment. These were basic clarification questions about my medical testing, yet she became increasingly impatient and irritated with me.

She then told me that one of the tests required an additional payment. I said that I had thought everything on the requisition was covered by OHIP and asked for clarification. Her response was, “Do it or not.” I was genuinely shocked by how dismissive and rude that response was. When I asked which test required payment, she told me to “read it myself.”

At that point, I chose to leave. I came to the clinic for medical testing and was simply asking reasonable questions about the instructions on my requisition, the timing of the tests, and the associated cost. I was not being confrontational or demanding, and I had been patient from the moment I arrived.

Patients should be able to ask basic questions about their medical testing without being made to feel as though they are an annoyance. I ultimately left without having my tests completed because I did not feel I should have to tolerate being spoken to in such a disrespectful and dismissive manner just to receive medical services. The receptionist’s attitude and lack of basic professionalism were completely unacceptable and should be addressed by the clinic.

I’m really disappointed with my experience at this salon, specifically with the makeup application. At $110, this is not an inexpensive service, and I was expecting the experience and results to be above and beyond.

I’ll start by admitting that I should have spoken up more while I was there. I kept telling myself that it “wasn’t that bad” and that I would eventually like it, but unfortunately, once I left and really looked at the makeup, I was extremely disappointed.

I specifically told the stylist at the beginning that I wanted a more natural look. However, the foundation used was way, WAY too dark for my skin tone. I was also surprised to see the same foundation being used on three different people. It was not blended down onto my neck at all, which left a very noticeable and intense line between my face and neck.

The eye makeup was another major issue. I had asked for false lashes to be applied over my extensions. When the stylist wasn’t able to do that, she offered mascara and eyeliner instead. I specifically declined the mascara because I knew it would cause my extensions to clump together. She then attempted the eyeliner, but there was a large gap that she had to repeatedly try to correct. By the time it looked somewhat decent, about 50% of my eye was covered in eyeliner.

I honestly left feeling like a raccoon and was trying very hard to convince myself that I liked it. I kept telling myself it wasn’t that bad, but I knew I wasn’t happy with it.

I ended up coming home and removing all of the makeup. Thankfully, I had brought my own makeup with me and was able to create a semi-decent look myself for the wedding.

I will say that the one redeeming factor of the appointment was the hair. I asked for a very specific style of curl, and I was actually really happy with the result. The hair turned out exactly how I was hoping it would, so I do want to give credit where it’s deserved.

I understand that makeup is subjective and that not every application will be perfect, but for $110, I expected much more attention to detail, especially when I had clearly communicated the natural look I was hoping for.

Unfortunately, this experience left me feeling like I had paid a significant amount of money for a service that I was genuinely unhappy with. I really hope the salon takes this feedback seriously, because I would hate for someone else to leave feeling the way I did.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but I believe it's important to share my experience.

First, booking an appointment was complicated, and when we finally arrived, the appointment started late again—by ​​more than 30 minutes. The owner herself did the haircut.

I also expected a truly child-friendly experience. Simply using cars as hairdressing chairs isn't enough, in my opinion, to call yourself "kid-friendly."

What disappointed me most was the attitude towards my 3-year-old, who was afraid of the clippers. Instead of being patient and understanding, several comments were made, including comparing him to other children who "do it well." As a parent, I felt judged and guilty because we don't go to the hairdresser often enough.

At the end of the haircut, my child was also refused his candy because he hadn't cooperated enough. He was also forbidden from touching the films available for children because he was crying during the screening.

A 3-year-old can be afraid of clippers. He might cry, fidget, or need time to adjust. It's precisely at these times that I expect to find patience, attentiveness, and kindness in a salon that presents itself as child-friendly.

I left without saying anything at the time, but I was deeply disappointed and stunned by this experience. For me, this type of approach is simply unacceptable, especially when young children are involved.

Unfortunately, we won't be going back.

I shop at this location fairly often and have always had positive experiences with the staff. During my most recent visit, everyone was exceptionally kind, helpful and professional. Unfortunately, the volume of the music made the overall shopping experience extremely unpleasant.

The music was so loud that I could barely hear employees speaking to me, had to raise my voice to respond, and noticed staff struggling to communicate with each other through their headsets. The speakers directly above the cash made it particularly difficult to hear while checking out.

When I politely mentioned the volume, I was very disappointed to learn that staff are apparently required to keep it at that level and have previously been reprimanded for lowering it. Employees also shared that the constant volume has caused headaches and migraines during their shifts. That is deeply concerning and not an acceptable working environment.

I purchased approximately $350 worth of clothing and genuinely love everything I bought, but I came very close to putting everything down and leaving because the noise was so overwhelming. I can only imagine how inaccessible this environment may be for customers with sensory sensitivities, migraines or hearing difficulties.

The employees at this location deserve recognition for providing excellent service under those conditions. I strongly encourage whoever controls the music policy to reconsider it for the wellbeing of both staff and customers.

one_star_reviews.text:
October 1, 2026
In the summer of 2021, our neighbor had the product Vipeq Thermal Corkshield put on their house by Innovative Cork.
After seeing how fantastic our neighbor’s house looked, we decided to have ours done as well. Our project was completed in August 2022. However, the installer at the time took a shortcut. He was supposed to power-wash the house first, but skipped this step. Because our stucco had a powdery layer on it, the product failed to adhere properly.
During the winter of 2022–2023, the CorkShield coating began peeling across our entire house. We contacted Innovative Cork, who inspected the property and determined that the original contractor failed to wash the house prior to application. As a result, the entire home required a complete re-application of the CorkShield.
Our wait lasted from mid-2023 until the fall of 2025, when Innovative Cork finally arrived to complete the warranty work. The process required scraping away the peeling areas, applying a clear liquid sealant, and reapplying the Corkshield. However, because they did not bring enough product to finish the job properly, they skimped on the wall that is less visible from the street.
Back in 2025, we complained that patches of the scraped wall and the clear liquid coating were still visible. We again contacted Innovative Cork.
Due to our persistence, Innovative Cork finally returned to redo the wall in the fall of 2026. However, they only agreed to use a single pail of product. While we hope this will be sufficient, it remains uncertain whether one pail is actually enough to complete the job properly.
We strongly advise against using Innovative Cork. While the final product appears to be fine when applied correctly, the customer service experience was exhausting. They are the sole provider of this product in Winnipeg, meaning you have no other options if things go wrong. In our case, it took 3.5 years to get a response and an additional year to finalize the warranty work. Hire them at your own risk.

one_star_reviews.text:
Warning about Richard and RGH Contracting. We hired him for a basic deck build. The whole thing just 2-3 feet off the ground. His work is careless, incompetent, and dangerous and he left the job half done. We had to hire someone else to fix his work and continue to completion.

Just one example of his incompetence: He attached the joists to the SIDES of the deck posts instead of resting them on top. This put the full weight of the deck on the fasteners between joist and post. What did he use to fasten? Six small nails (see photo). This was done in several places. Despite sounding like an experienced contractor, only a careless and incompetent person would this and many other things he did.

Some other issues that are no less serious: His crew stole several large pavers from our yard. We have it on video. This was very upsetting for us. Although this wasn’t even the reason we called the RCMP on him. We now understand why he asked if he could cover our cameras while he worked. Richard also brought his girlfriend to the job site to hang out without us knowing.

one_star_reviews.text:
A disappointing end to 15 years as a loyal customer.

I have been a client of Michael’s Hair Body Mind for approximately 15 years, primarily for colour and haircuts, and until this experience I had always been very happy with the quality of their services. In fact, I have recommended the salon and continued returning year after year because of that trust.

Unfortunately, my most recent colour experience was very different.

I had a colour service in June that I loved. When I returned in July, I specifically asked to refresh and lighten my existing blonde highlights. Instead, my hair was taken significantly darker and turned a coppery/red tone that was completely different from what I had requested and from the beautiful result I had received just weeks earlier. I had to return the following morning for a corrective service, for which I was charged an additional $107 + HST.

The colour continued to deteriorate, so I contacted the salon to express my concerns and ask for the matter to be resolved. What was particularly disappointing was the customer service that followed. I was promised return calls on three separate occasions: July 31, August 1, and August 4. None of those calls happened.

Only after emailing the owner Lina did I receive a response, and from the new salon/office manager Shauna Dawson. After promising to reach out to me twice, Ms. Dawson also failed to make this a priority or to contact me. Through a brief text message exchange, I politely confronted her about this, and my belief that as a customer ignored by her team for over a week, she should have been making contact with me a top priority. Rather than discussing how to correct the colour issue or addressing my concerns about my customer experience and the additional charge, I was emailed by Shauna the next day that the salon had decided that they were "not the right salon to continue providing my hair services" and that they would no longer book appointments for me.

They refunded the $107 corrective-service charge, which I appreciate. However, the refund does not change the larger issue: After approximately 15 years as a loyal customer, this is how this salon chose to handle a customer who raised a legitimate concern for the first time about a service she was unhappy with.

What I find particularly disappointing is the broader message this sends about customer service. I believe customers should be able to respectfully express dissatisfaction, ask questions, and assert reasonable boundaries about the services they receive without being characterized as a problem customer simply because they did so.

In today's service environment, customer loyalty should mean something. When any customer, let alone a 15-year long customer, raises a legitimate concern, I would expect the response to be listening, problem-solving and finding a reasonable resolution, not simply deciding that the customer is no longer welcome.

This is the first and only negative review I have ever posted on Google. For a salon I truly liked, as their customer of 15 years. And rightly so, it will also be my last experience with this salon.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Iconic Beauty Aesthetics.

I purchased a SkinCeuticals Silymarin CF from them for $144. Although the product was discounted, the website did not disclose that it was expired. I only discovered the expiration issue after receiving the product.

What is especially upsetting is not simply receiving an expired product—it is how the situation was handled afterward. I contacted Iconic Beauty Aesthetics expecting a reasonable resolution, such as a refund, but my request was ignored.

A discount does not make it acceptable to sell an expired skincare product without clearly informing the customer of its expiration date. SkinCeuticals products are expensive, and $144 is certainly not an insignificant amount of money. If a product is expired, that information should be clearly and prominently disclosed before the customer makes the purchase, so they can make an informed decision.

I was particularly surprised by this experience because Iconic Beauty Aesthetics has such an impressive collection of reviews and a strong reputation. That reputation is precisely why I felt comfortable purchasing from them in the first place. Unfortunately, my experience left me feeling that the transaction was misleading and unfair.

I would have expected a business selling high-end skincare to be transparent about the condition and expiration of its products and to take responsibility when a customer receives an expired item.

I hope the company reconsiders its position and understands that transparency and fair treatment matter far more than the sale of a single product. Customers deserve to know exactly what they are paying for—especially when spending $144 on skincare.

G adventures doesn't care about the trips they promise just selling as many tours as possible.

What's the point in even having tour physical ratings if they will sell it to anyone and then change it after the fact.

To summarize if you are younger 20s to 40s avoid G Adventures or ask about your exact tour demographics ahead of time because instead of the fun active tour you were promised it may just be a trip with your complaining grand parents that becomes short slow day trips that end early cutting out the promised iternery, a taxi ride back to the hotel and go to bed early.

I am extremely disappointed with my daughter’s haircut.

We came in with a very clear reference photo showing exactly the style my daughter wanted. I completely understood that her hair was not as long as the hair in the reference photo, so I did not expect the finished cut to have the same overall length. However, she absolutely had enough hair to create the same general shape and style while preserving much more of the length she already had.

Instead, Sandra cut her hair extremely short, particularly around the sides and back, and the finished haircut looked nothing like the photo we provided.

After the haircut, Sandra tried to explain that my daughter’s hair had not been long enough to achieve the style in the photo and that it would grow into the style!!!  If she truly believed the requested style could not be achieved with my daughter’s existing hair, that should have been explained BEFORE she started cutting. We could have discussed what was realistically possible, agreed on an alternative, or simply chosen not to proceed. Instead, that explanation came after the length was already gone. The cut cannot be corrected.

My daughter is incredibly upset. I washed and restyled her hair myself when we got home and was able to make it look somewhat better than it did when we left the salon, but it still is not remotely the haircut she asked for.

She is so unhappy and uncomfortable with how short her hair was cut that I am now having to spend additional money to buy her a wig so that she can feel good about herself while her hair grows back.

Hair does grow back, but that does not undo how a young girl feels when she looks in the mirror and sees a haircut she never asked for. We brought a reference photo specifically to make what she wanted clear. If it could not be done, we should have been told that before her hair was cut.

This experience has been incredibly upsetting and disappointing.

To Whom It May Concern:

Re:

I am writing regarding two EFI Versa Chill refrigeration units that Gray’s Food Service purchased and picked up from your warehouse in May 2026. Unfortunately, both units were found to have damage and/or operational issues at the time of pickup, and despite bringing these issues to your attention immediately, they remain unresolved.

1. Versa Chill 3 Glass Door Worktop Fridge

Model: 1009/CWDR3-772VCX

The packaging appeared to be in good condition when we inspected the unit. However, when the fridge was unboxed at your warehouse, we discovered two holes in the rear panel that appear to have been caused by forklift forks.

In addition, the side grill covering the compressor was damaged, and the refrigerator has not been cooling properly since we received it.

2. 60” Freezer Worktop Stainless Steel 2 Door

Model: 1009/FWD22-60VCX

Again, the packaging appeared to be in good condition when we inspected the unit. Once the freezer was unboxed at your warehouse, we discovered damage to the exterior of the right-hand door.

More importantly, when the freezer door is opened, the door falls off, making the unit unusable for its intended purpose.

Initial Notification

These issues were brought to the attention of Sales Representative **Jason Iwanoczko at the time of pickup**. Photographs of the damage, along with the serial numbers for both units, were provided to Jason that same day.

At the time, Jason advised us that he would take care of the issues as soon as possible. He also indicated that if we took the damaged units with us, he would arrange a discount/credit on the two refrigerators to compensate for the issues.

We relied on those assurances and took possession of the equipment.

Lack of Response

It is now **August 20, 2026**, several months after the original purchase and notification, and our busy summer operating season is nearly over. Despite numerous attempts to contact Jason by **text message, telephone, and email**, we have received no meaningful response or resolution.

We have been dealing with these issues **since the day the equipment was picked up**, and it is extremely frustrating that equipment we paid for in full has remained damaged and, in the case of the freezer, essentially unusable, without the matter being properly addressed.

We are including the original photographs taken at the time of pickup, along with the serial numbers, to document the condition of the equipment when it was received.

We are therefore requesting that **Russell Hendrix provide us, in writing, with a clear explanation of how you intend to resolve these outstanding damage and warranty claims**, including:

* Repair or replacement of the damaged components;
* Resolution of the cooling issue with the Versa Chill refrigerator;
* Repair of the freezer door so the unit can be safely and properly used;
* The previously discussed credit/discount for the damaged equipment; and
* A specific timeline for when these issues will be resolved.

Additional Outstanding Request

We also contacted Jason regarding our desire to purchase a **new grill and a chef's base for delivery in late June 2026**. That request was also left unanswered, and we have received no follow-up regarding the equipment.

We have been a customer who expected reasonable communication and support following the purchase of this equipment. Unfortunately, the lack of response over the past several months has left us with damaged equipment, an unusable freezer, and an unresolved warranty claim during our operating season.

We would appreciate having this matter escalated to the appropriate person at Russell Hendrix and ask that you **respond as soon as possible with a clear plan and timeline for resolution**.

We look forward to resolving this matter promptly.

Sincerely,

Tyler Gray
Operations Manager

Grand Beach Boardwalk, Manitoba

I usually make a point of playing Eagle Point whenever I’m travelling through Kamloops. It’s a course I’ve always enjoyed, with great views and a layout that can be quite challenging.

There was no communication when we booked, or when we checked in, that the tee boxes and greens were being punched. What was even more disappointing was that we were charged the full regular rate, with no consideration given to the significant impact the maintenance work had on the overall golfing experience. Had we been informed ahead of time that the course was undergoing this work, we would have chosen to play somewhere else.

I understand that course maintenance is necessary, but I feel customers should be made aware of significant maintenance activities before booking, especially when they substantially affect the quality of the round.

Overall, I was very disappointed with the experience, particularly because I have played Eagle Point several times and have always enjoyed the course in the past.

one_star_reviews.text:
You're asking for something much more severe—something that communicates that, in your view, **management has allowed the institution to cease functioning as a proper library**. I can make it much sharper without weakening it with attacks based on nationality or homelessness itself.

What has happened to the Vancouver Public Library is an absolute disgrace.

This institution is called a public **library**, yet management appears to have abandoned even the most basic expectation associated with that word: providing an environment in which people can read, study, research, and work without being surrounded by constant noise, disorder, intoxication, and disruption.

The conditions I have repeatedly witnessed are unacceptable.

People conduct loud telephone conversations as though they were sitting in a coffee shop. Patrons openly talk at volumes completely inappropriate for a library. Even staff members engage in conversations loud enough to disturb people attempting to concentrate. Meanwhile, individuals who appear severely intoxicated or under the influence of drugs are routinely present, and behavior that should trigger immediate intervention seems instead to have become normalized.

Then there is security.

One security guard repeatedly bangs on washroom doors with an object during checks, creating an obnoxious noise that carries through the library. Think about the absurdity of that: the very people supposedly employed to maintain an orderly environment are themselves creating disturbances.

What exactly is management doing?

The problem is not that homeless people use the library. Homeless people have every right to use a public library **when they follow the same reasonable standards of behavior expected of everybody else**. The problem is allowing intoxication, drug-related behavior, excessive noise, disruption, and antisocial conduct to overwhelm the legitimate function of the building.

Compassion does not require turning a library into chaos.

Inclusiveness does not mean eliminating standards.

And tolerating virtually everything is not competent management.

At some point, Vancouver Public Library management needs to admit what this facility has become. Based on what I have repeatedly witnessed, it increasingly resembles a **poorly controlled drop-in center that happens to contain books**, rather than a professionally operated public library.

A library is not a homeless shelter.

It is not a detoxification center.

It is not a bar.

It is not a social club.

It is not a place where people should be free to shout across rooms or conduct loud telephone conversations.

And it certainly should not be a place where patrons attempting to study are expected to tolerate disruption created by the library's own security personnel.

**IT IS A LIBRARY.**

That distinction apparently needs to be rediscovered.

There are students trying to earn degrees. There are people researching, studying, applying for employment, learning new skills, reading, and trying to improve their lives. Some of those people have nowhere else suitable to work. Yet they are expected to tolerate an environment that management would presumably never accept in its own administrative offices.

Vancouver taxpayers fund this institution. They have every right to expect competent management, professional security, reasonable quiet, basic order, and behavioral standards that are actually enforced.

Stop pretending that enforcing reasonable standards is somehow incompatible with compassion.

Stop allowing disruptive behavior to dictate the environment for everyone else.

Stop expecting serious library users to simply tolerate it.

And start operating the Vancouver Public Library as an actual **library**.

Because right now, in my experience, it is failing at the most fundamental function contained in its own name.
Half a star.

one_star_reviews.text:
At first, this restoration company was great. They called us right away, came to our home promptly, and seemed to do everything they were “supposed” to do. Unfortunately, that was 5 weeks ago.

Since they found out we would not be using them for the repairs, it has felt as though our claim was moved to the bottom of the priority list.

My biggest concern is that it has now been 5 weeks since they first came to our home, and despite having been back four additional times, they STILL have not submitted their report to our insurance company. Our insurance company has now put our claim “on hold” until they receive this report. Five weeks later, we are still waiting for something that is preventing us from moving forward with the repair process.

Communication has also been extremely frustrating. We have had to call MULTIPLE times to have the dehumidifiers they left in our home picked up, and we have repeatedly followed up regarding the sanitization spray. We finally heard back yesterday, and the spray is now scheduled for today.

After another phone call today, I was told that a “formal complaint” has officially been made and will be sent to “everyone,” and that I should receive a call “soon.” At this point, unfortunately, I am not very confident that will happen without another follow up from us.

It is incredibly disappointing. We experienced a devastating flood, lost so many of our family possessions, and are already dealing with the stress of trying to put our lives and home back together. Having to repeatedly chase a company that was supposed to help us through this process has only added to that stress.

The most frustrating part is that we were referred to this company as a vetted restoration company from our insurance company Intact, and we expected much better communication, urgency, and follow through.

We simply want their report submitted so our insurance company can do its job and we can finally start moving forward.
